items.text: The source was a manual spreadsheet upload, not an automated process: a single named file was loaded, and no automated process anywhere in this project's material loads or mentions this table
The store and department fields are plain text codes, not formally linked to the store or department dimensions, unlike almost every other similar table analysed in this project

This table holds a single one-time event, not an ongoing load: every row was created within the same couple of seconds in late November 2021, all for the same single business day (a Saturday before Thanksgiving), the same premium type, and the same reporting scenario, one row per store. It has not been touched since
No invalid keys and no duplicate records were found across all rows

blocks.text: Still open, not confirmed in code or data yet. None of this blocks the lineage above, it is tracked here so nothing gets forgotten.

items.text: Whether Weis still needs one-off holiday premium pay reporting of this kind, given it has not recurred since the single 2021 load, is unconfirmed
items.note: This table has no automated process to migrate: it is a single manual upload, so the migration decision is really whether to preserve the historical rows as a reference, or to build a real recurring process if this reporting need still exists
